Full-source review finds the candidate factually accurate, precise, and appropriately bounded about what this overview does not define. Two evidence-completeness omissions prevent approval. Full-source review confirms the permanent and immediate Metronome-invoice void description, POST route, global bearer security, UUID field formats, operation ID, and the separately documented downstream-manual boundary. The raw SHA-256 matches the trusted order; canonical_url and raw_files are exact; the path-qualified raw backlink and all related wikilinks resolve; the source target is absent; candidate.md equals receipt.source_page; suggestions.json equals receipt.suggestions; both concept anchors exist; and the submitted quote text is faithful at the stated locations. Two factual schema-boundary errors and one completeness omission prevent approval. The OpenAPI operation does not mark requestBody itself required; it marks id required only inside the body object schema. The HTTP 200 schema defines a top-level data property without requiring it, then requires id only inside data; the example contains data.id, but the schema does not guarantee that top-level property. The candidate and durable concept update instead describe the whole request and data.id response as required or returned guarantees and say the response includes no status, where the source only documents an example and a schema whose listed nested field is id. The candidate also omits the operation description's explicit intended uses: correcting billing errors, cancelling incorrect charges, and handling disputed invoices that should not be collected. Finally, the grounding excerpts do not cover global security application, operationId, or either example, despite candidate claims based on those locations. No contradiction callout, new concept, comparison, company update, index update, log update, or additional shared target is otherwise required; the reciprocal invoicing source link is valid.
